sections.h2: Historic Franklin: Main Street, the Square and the old neighborhoods
paragraphs: Franklin's downtown is one of the best-preserved historic districts in Tennessee, and the trees around it are part of the picture. Main Street and the Public Square, with the Williamson County Courthouse at their center, are surrounded by older residential blocks where large oaks, maples and hickories stand beside homes that have been there for well over a century. Carter House, Carnton and the other Civil War sites that dot the area sit among mature trees too, and Pinkerton Park and Harlinsdale Farm add more big old trees along their edges.

Close to downtown, lots are tight and the trees are old, so removals are done in controlled sections rather than dropped whole, and cleanup has to be careful and complete. Many owners here want a tree preserved if at all possible, so we are glad to look at crown cleaning, selective thinning and hazard reduction before recommending removal. If a tree is dead, diseased or leaning toward a structure, we explain the safest way to take it down and what the job includes.

sections.h2: Cool Springs, Westhaven, Berry Farms and Fieldstone Farms
paragraphs: Away from downtown, Franklin has grown quickly. Cool Springs, Westhaven, Berry Farms and Fieldstone Farms were built in recent decades on land that was cleared and graded, and they share a set of tree problems. Builders plant inexpensive, fast-growing trees close to foundations, driveways and patios, and young trees that were never structurally pruned develop weak, V-shaped crotches that split in wind. Trees saved from the original land often decline a few years after construction because their roots were cut or compacted.

Most of these neighborhoods have HOAs, and many have rules on removing or replacing trees, so check your covenants before scheduling a removal. Common calls include dead trees standing near houses and fences, builder-planted trees outgrowing their spots and crowded plantings that need thinning.

sections.h2: Leiper's Fork, Thompson's Station and the open county
paragraphs: West and south of town, around Leiper's Fork and Thompson's Station, properties get larger and the trees get bigger. Old oaks and hickories stand in pastures and along fence lines, and tree lines along property edges may never have been thinned. Larger lots bring bigger jobs: long driveways, tall trees far from the road and brush that needs clearing before a barn, a pool or a new drive goes in. Those calls often combine removal, stump grinding and land clearing in a single visit.

Open land gives wind room to build, and big trees in open pastures have no neighbors to shelter them. A lean that is getting worse, cracks in the trunk or where a big limb meets it, mushrooms around the base and large dead branches high in the crown are all reasons to have a tree inspected before the next storm.

sections.h2: Before you remove a tree in Franklin
paragraphs: Whether you need approval depends on the property. Franklin has development standards and historic overlay districts, and HOAs can add their own requirements. Street trees and trees in the public right-of-way cannot be removed by a homeowner or contractor. Check with the City of Franklin and your HOA before removing a large tree, and confirm current requirements, since rules can change.

Look up before work begins. Trees touching or close to power lines should be handled by the utility or a qualified line-clearance crew, and anyone in danger should call 911. If stump grinding or digging is involved, call Tennessee 811 so buried utilities are marked. We point out lines, fences, septic fields and structures when we quote.

We are a locally owned, licensed and insured company based in Nashville. For Franklin jobs we give a free estimate, explain how the tree will come down and what the price includes, remove it safely and haul the debris away. Stump grinding can be added on the same visit, and storm damage and emergency removal are available when a tree is already down. If trimming will do the job, we will tell you.
